rationale: This is the final iteration, so the design should be the most robust one the evidence supports, not an untested step. Iteration 8 is the best measured design (913.46): oval 20/20, s-bend 20/20, slalom 18/20, with steering oscillation 0.24 to 0.32, well under the 0.5 warning level. Iteration 9 narrowed wheel_track to 0.11 m and lost 3 slalom finishes (15/20, control effort 15.1), and iteration 10 reverted to the iteration 8 design and reproduced its score exactly, so the result is repeatable. Sensor y = 0.08 m is the top of the allowed range, so the phase-lead lever is used up. The remaining loss is the slalom tail (2 off-track ends), and the per-track ceiling is about 940 to 950 on the time and progress terms. I considered kd 1.7 (hypothesis a from iteration 10) or base_speed 1.25, but both are untested, and the expected gain is about 1 to 2 points against a risk of losing oval or s-bend completion on the unseen track. So I submit the iteration 8 geometry and controller unchanged. Expected result: a score near 913 on the development tracks, with slalom finishes of 16 to 19 of 20. The measurements requested below will show whether slalom failures are overshoot or lost authority, which would guide any later revision.
